title: Is Walmart Stock Increasing Your Market Risk?

Investors often hold Walmart (WMT) stock alongside funds that already track the S&P 500. Walmart is a retailer of groceries and everyday essentials worth about $886 billion. A stock that moves in lockstep with the broader index simply compounds existing bets, while one that charts its own course helps spread risk. So what does Walmart stock do on the market's good days and bad days?

Walmart Stock Has Gone Its Own Way

Over the past year, Walmart shares have not compounded broader market risk. Consider a $10,000 position in Walmart stock. On an average day when the S&P 500 rose over the past year, the index gained 0.65% while the retail shares ended the day about $1 lower. Conversely, on an average day when the index fell, the index dropped 0.6% and the shares finished about $10 higher. Distilled to a single metric, Walmart stock moved about 0.04% in the opposite direction for each 1% the index moved. That translates to almost no link at all.

This lack of correlation does not mean the investment is calm. Over the past year, its volatility, defined as the size of its typical swings, was 27%, against 13.0% for the S&P 500. Walmart swung about twice as widely as the benchmark index, yet it did not move in step with it. Holding the stock introduces risk, but it remains a separate one from the risk embedded in index funds.

Can Walmart's Steady Sales Prolong This Pattern?

The underlying business suggests this pattern will persist, with the stock trading on company-specific developments rather than broader market sentiment. Over the past year, Walmart's correlation with the index, a measure of how often the two move together, was -0.02. That means the two barely move together.

Operations remain steady. Revenue grew between 5.6% and 7.3% from a year earlier in each of the past four quarters. During the company's August 20, 2026 earnings call, management raised its forecast for sales growth in the current fiscal year, measured in constant currency. Executives now expect a range of 4% to 5%, up from prior estimates of 3.5% to 4.5%.

Investors pay a high price for that stability. Walmart stock is priced at 40.1 times earnings, against the 21.9 multiple for the S&P 500. On that same call, management acknowledged that lapping 19% growth in earnings per share will be a challenge next year. Given its current valuation, a disappointing quarter could trigger sharp price movements regardless of how the broader market performs. Consequently, wide swings of its own are likely to continue.

title: Should You Buy Target Stock At This Price?
detail:
Should You Buy Target Stock At This Price?
Trefis Team

TGT
WMT
AMZN
COST
HD
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure
Image from Pixabay

Shares of Target (TGT) currently trade at 15.9 times earnings, below the 21.9 multiple for the median S&P 500 company, though one-time tariff refunds flatter that figure. This valuation gap persists even after the stock returned 80% over the past twelve months. The disconnect suggests one of two scenarios: either a fundamentally sound retailer remains on sale, or the broader market doubts Target can sustain its recent results. So what does a buyer actually get at this price?

Target Is Drawing More Shoppers

First, investors acquire a retailer that is growing its top line again. During fiscal Q2 2026, Target generated net sales of $26.5 billion, representing a 5.3% increase from a year earlier. Comparable sales rose 3.8%, driven by a higher volume of shoppers. Store traffic rose 3.6%, while the average ticket was about flat.

Buyers also acquire a strong cash generator. Over the last twelve months, Target's operations brought in $8.7 billion of cash, about twice its $4.4 billion of net income. At its current price, the stock costs 8.0 times that operating cash flow, against the 14.7 multiple for the S&P 500. Judged purely on the past year, Target resembles a growing business that successfully converts profit into cash while trading at a below-market multiple.

How Has Target Done Over Three Years?

Over three years, Target has not grown at all. Although Target grew its revenue by 2.0% over the last twelve months, its three-year average shows a decline of 0.1% a year. That average reflects consecutive top-line drops. Revenue fell 1.5% in the prior twelve months, following a decline of 0.7% in the twelve months before that.

Target's weak spots are the home and apparel categories. During Target's latest full fiscal year, home furnishings revenue fell 6.5%, and apparel and accessories revenue fell 4.7%. Each of these two categories accounts for about 15% of the company's revenue.

Furthermore, recent profit benefited from a temporary boost. Target earned $4.11 a share in fiscal Q2 2026, but tariff refunds supplied $1.65 of that total. Excluding the refunds, earnings per share were still about 20% higher than a year earlier. Management's full-year guidance does not count on any more refunds. Yet even with those refunds included, Target recorded an operating margin of 5.6% over the last twelve months, against the 18.5% margin for the median S&P 500 company. Given the flat three-year record and the absence of future refunds in the guidance, the current stock price appears to reflect market skepticism that recent improvements will last.

title: Walmart's Fulfillment Center to Boost West Coast Delivery Reach

Walmart's Fulfillment Center to Boost West Coast Delivery Reach
Vrishali Bagree

WMT
TGT
COST

Trading disclosure

Walmart Inc. WMT continues to strengthen its omnichannel capabilities through investments in supply-chain automation, technology and faster delivery services. These initiatives are supporting e-commerce growth and enhancing customer convenience. Reinforcing these efforts, Walmart recently opened its fifth next-generation fulfillment center in Stockton, CA, to expand delivery capabilities across the West Coast.

The new facility spans more than 900,000 square feet and is expected to create more than 1,000 jobs. Strategically located in California's Central Valley, the center expands Walmart's fulfillment capacity closer to West Coast customers. This should help the retailer improve delivery speed, strengthen order-processing capabilities and support growing online demand.

The facility incorporates advanced automation, machine learning and a high-density storage system to streamline operations. Its technology reduces the traditional 12-step fulfillment process to five steps, potentially improving productivity and order-handling efficiency. Together with Walmart's broader fulfillment network, these advanced facilities are expected to enable next- or two-day shipping coverage for 95% of the U.S. population.

The expansion aligns with Walmart's strong digital momentum. In second-quarter fiscal 2027, Walmart U.S. e-commerce sales increased 24%, while Marketplace sales grew 52%. Nearly half of Marketplace sales flowed through Walmart Fulfillment Services. More than 50% of the company's e-commerce fulfillment volume was processed through automated facilities, reflecting progress in supply-chain modernization.

The Stockton investment should further strengthen Walmart's fulfillment network, support Marketplace growth and improve operational efficiency over time. However, higher capital spending and related depreciation expenses remain important considerations as the retailer continues expanding its automated infrastructure.

What Do the Latest Metrics Say About Walmart?

Walmart, which competes with Costco Wholesale Corporation COST and Target Corporation TGT, has seen its shares gain 9% over the past year compared with the industry's breakeven performance. Shares of Costco have climbed 1.2%, while Target has surged 75.9% in the aforementioned period.

title: Can Ads and Subscriptions Justify Walmart’s (WMT) Premium Valuation?
detail:
Can Ads and Subscriptions Justify Walmart’s (WMT) Premium Valuation?
Maham Fatima
Mon, October 12, 2026 at 7:30 AM PDT 5 min read
WMT
Trade Walmart on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Walmart's shoppers come for low prices. Its shareholders are paying anything but. Investors now hand over about 38.59 times expected earnings for Walmart (NASDAQ:WMT), a higher price than the stock has averaged over the past five years and far above what the broader consumer staples sector commands.

The business itself needs little introduction. Walmart sells groceries, household goods, and general merchandise through US supercenters, Sam's Club warehouses, and international operations such as India's Flipkart, earning thin margins on enormous volume. WMT also ranks fourth on our list of the 10 Best Bear Market Stocks to Invest In Right Now. Increasingly, though, it makes money from things shoppers never put in a cart: advertising, membership fees, and digital services built on top of its stores. Is this still a grocery stock wearing a tech-stock multiple, or has the profit engine genuinely changed? The answer hinges on how much of Walmart's recent earnings growth comes from that new business, and how much came from a one-time boost.

Can Ads and Subscriptions Justify Walmart’s (WMT) Premium Valuation?
Scale Pays Twice

Walmart's original moat is scale. Its buying power keeps prices low, and its store network puts much of America within easy reach of a pickup counter or delivery van. That combination still pulls people in. In fiscal Q2 2027, Walmart US transactions rose 1.5%, and Sam's Club transactions climbed 7.0%.

What's changed is how much that traffic is worth. Every shopper browsing the app or website is an audience advertisers will pay to reach, and global advertising revenue jumped 38% in the quarter. Global e-commerce sales grew 23%, while membership fee revenue rose 17%. It's the same flywheel that turned Amazon's advertising arm into a profit powerhouse, which brings us to another question: Is the Market Underestimating Amazon's Moat?

These streams earn far fatter margins than selling detergent. That's why consolidated operating income rose 17.4% on an adjusted, constant-currency basis, on revenue growth of 5.9%.

A Raise With Fine Print

Management lifted its full-year outlook alongside those results. It now expects fiscal 2027 net sales to grow 4.0% to 5.0% in constant currency, up from 3.5% to 4.5%, and adjusted EPS of $2.80 to $2.87, up from $2.75 to $2.85.

The nearer-term picture is softer. Fiscal Q3 guidance calls for sales growth of 3.0% to 3.75% and operating income growth of just 2.0% to 4.0%. Part of that is timing: Flipkart's Big Billion Days sale shifts into the fourth quarter, which management says shaves more than 100 basis points off Q3 sales growth. CFO John David Rainey asked investors to judge Q2 and Q3 together for a cleaner read.

title: What Cheaper Gas Would Mean For Costco’s Sales And Margins
detail:
What Cheaper Gas Would Mean For Costco’s Sales And Margins
Trefis Team

TGT

Image from Pixabay

Costco Wholesale (COST) stock currently trades at 45.6 times earnings, compared with 21.9 for the S&P 500. Investors paying that price may be counting on growth. That growth has materialized, as September net sales rose 13.0% from a year earlier. However, gas hit $4.32 a gallon in mid-September, and those higher fuel costs add to Costco's sales. So how much of that growth would go if gas prices came back down?

How Much Of Costco's Sales Growth Comes From Gas?

Gas price inflation lifted Costco's sales by approximately 3% in fiscal Q4 2026, management said on the September 24, 2026 call. Comparable sales rose 9.4% that quarter, but the increase was 6.7% once gas prices and currency were taken out.

Gas itself grew much faster than the rest of the business. Management put the rise in comparable gas sales in the mid-30s percent, noting that the increase came from a higher price per gallon alongside record volumes.

September's sales also faced scrutiny. Citing a Wall Street analyst, Barron's reported on October 8, 2026, that part of the monthly jump in comparable sales came from one-off, lower-margin boosters.

The underlying drivers of expensive gas could change. Management tied the higher cost of gas and motor oil to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. They also cautioned that the situation is still uncertain, and that inflation is difficult to predict.

Expensive Gas Lowered Costco's Margin Rate In Fiscal Q4

While cheaper gas would lower Costco's sales, it would probably lift its margin rate. The retailer's reported gross margin rate fell 11 basis points from a year earlier in fiscal Q4 2026, landing at 11.02%. Excluding gas inflation, management said the rate was 20 basis points higher than a year earlier.

The stock itself may be more exposed than the underlying profit. Costco's P/E has ranged from 26.8 to 56.0 over the past ten years, placing today's multiple in the upper half of that historical range. Buyers paying that much have less room for a slower sales figure. Costco stock has fallen sharply in the past. In 2022, it dropped 31% from peak to trough, against a 25% peak-to-trough decline for the S&P 500.

Outside Gas, Costco's Warehouses Are Still Growing

Shopping frequency rose 3.3% worldwide in fiscal Q4 2026, and management said sales excluding gas remain very robust. Members are also renewing their memberships. The renewal rate in the U.S. and Canada was 92.3%, up 10 basis points from the quarter before.

Costco's broader finances are not the issue either. The company generated an operating profit over the last twelve months that was 80.6 times its interest expense.

Costco's 19% September Digital Sales Growth Signals Strong Momentum

Costco Wholesale Corporation COST continued to demonstrate solid momentum across its digital operations in September 2026, reinforcing the strength of its online shopping ecosystem. The warehouse retailer reported a 19% year-over-year increase in digitally enabled sales for the five weeks ended Oct. 4, 2026. Excluding foreign exchange fluctuations, growth stood at 19.1%, suggesting that the reported jump was largely driven by underlying business activity rather than currency fluctuations.

The September results extend the healthy digital trends witnessed in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026, when digitally enabled comparable sales advanced 19.5%, or 19.8% on an adjusted basis. For the full fiscal year, digitally enabled comparable sales increased 20.9%, highlighting sustained demand for Costco's digital offerings.

Costco defines digitally enabled sales as transactions initiated through digital devices, regardless of whether orders are fulfilled through warehouses, distribution centers or Costco Travel.

Costco's ongoing digital improvements provide additional context for this momentum. During the fourth quarter, e-commerce website and app traffic increased 30%, while personalized initiatives generated triple-digit sales growth. Costco expanded its same-day delivery options through partnerships with Uber Eats and DoorDash, alongside its established Instacart relationship.

September's performance reflects the continuation of an established digital growth trend, supported by broader shopping access, improving personalization and stronger engagement across Costco's digital channels.

How Walmart & Target Are Scaling Digital Sales

Walmart Inc.'s WMT digital momentum remains strong, with global e-commerce sales rising 23% in second-quarter fiscal 2027 and accounting for 24% of total net sales. Walmart U.S. e-commerce grew 24%, supported by store-fulfilled delivery and marketplace expansion. Walmart also reported more than 40% growth in store-fulfilled deliveries, while fast delivery grew 48%, underscoring how Walmart is using speed, assortment and fulfillment density to deepen digital engagement.

Target Corporation TGT also posted healthy digital growth, with second-quarter fiscal 2026 comparable digital sales increasing 8.7%, led by more than 25% growth in same-day delivery. Target is supporting this momentum through digital personalization, AI-powered shopping tools and enhanced app experiences. Target's digital traffic from external AI platforms is also rising more than 3.5 times the industry rate, suggesting Target is increasingly using technology and convenience to strengthen online discovery and engagement.
